title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is not a manuscript page of the 1976 divided-power de Rham notes. It is a typed page, p. 185 of Exposé IX of SGA 7 I (Grothendieck, 'Modèles de Néron et monodromie', §13, the complex-analytic case). It is filed between handwritten pages on p-adic valuations of divided powers p^n/n!. The archive stamp reads 503 and the hand-numbered folio is 239. It was probably reused as scrap paper or misfiled.

Content, end of 13.5.3:
(a) Ends a statement that a morphism S'→S which is 'schematically dominant' in the sense that O_S → f_*(O_{S'}) is injective is a morphism of effective descent for the fibred category of relative abelian schemes. The start of the hypothesis is on the previous typed page, which is not provided.
(b) Suggests that the proof method of 13.5.2 (algebraization of analytic abelian schemes over a germ (S,s) from algebraizability of the formal completion) should extend to any analytic space B proper over S. It then poses the harder question: if X is proper analytic over S and its formal completion along X_s is algebraizable, is X algebraizable over S near s? Algebraizability is to be understood in the wider sense of coming from an algebraic space over O_{S,s} in Artin's sense, rather than a scheme as in [10].

13.5.4 (in the setting of 13.5.1):
- Fix the standard normalization μ_n ≅ (Z/nZ) over C via m ↦ exp(2πi m/n).
- Passing to the limit over powers of ℓ gives an identification Z_ℓ(1)_C ≅ Z_ℓ, used to identify the two sides.
- From the exact sequence (13.1.3) (the uniformization/exponential sequence for the analytic family), applying the long exact sequence of Ext^i_Z(Z/nZ, −) yields a canonical isomorphism, continued on the next typed page. Presumably this is the identification of the n-torsion, hence T_ℓ, with H_1 ⊗ Z/n, used to compare ℓ-adic and transcendental monodromy pairings.
errors: Minor directional slip: the map m ↦ exp(2iπm/n) goes from Z/nZ to μ_n, while the displayed isomorphism is written μ_n ≅ Z/nZ. This is harmless, since it is an isomorphism.
'standart' is a typo in the typescript for 'standard'.
This is not an error in the mathematics: the page belongs to SGA 7 Exposé IX, not to the divided-power de Rham notes (cote 136). Its placement here is archival.

ideas.what: Morphisms S'→S with O_S → f_*O_{S'} injective are effective descent morphisms for abelian schemes.
ideas.modern_name: Effective descent for abelian schemes along schematically dominant morphisms (Raynaud/Grothendieck-type extension results)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA 7 IX); related work by Raynaud

ideas.what: Question: a proper analytic space over a germ (S,s) whose formal completion along the special fibre is algebraizable — is it algebraizable near s, as an Artin algebraic space over O_{S,s}?
ideas.modern_name: Relative algebraization of analytic families / formal-to-analytic algebraization via Artin approximation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (question in SGA 7); Artin approximation and algebraization (Artin 1968–1970)

ideas.what: Normalization μ_n ≅ Z/n over C via exp(2πi m/n), giving Z_ℓ(1) ≅ Z_ℓ over C.
ideas.modern_name: Standard trivialization of the Tate twist over C

ideas.what: Ext(Z/n, −) applied to the uniformization exact sequence gives a canonical identification of n-torsion with H_1 ⊗ Z/n.
ideas.modern_name: Comparison of ℓ-adic Tate module with Betti homology

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a typescript page of the published SGA 7 Exposé IX (§13.5.3–13.5.4), misfiled or reused in the divided-power de Rham folder. All of its content is in print. The only curiosity is archival: an SGA 7 page sits among the 1975–76 crystalline/divided-power notes, perhaps as the reverse side of scrap paper.
